newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday July 15.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The Italian government and trades union leaders met late on Monday ahead of talks on reforming the country's pensions system. The government wants to cut social spending by seven trillion lire, some five trillion lire of which will come from pension cuts. (all)

* Italian Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said the 500 soldiers sent to restore order in Naples after a wave of Camorra mafia killings this year would stay as long as necessary. Prime Minister Romano Prodi had said the soldiers, who started their mission on Monday, would be home by Christmas. (Corriere della Sera).

* Negotiations between the European Commission and Italian flag carrier Alitalia on its recapitalistaion plans officially end on Tuesday. The airline will be allowed to go ahead with financing for 2.75 trillion lire in three tranches provided it reduces operations by 10 percent, or 27,000 flights a year. (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* National statistics institute ISTAT said in a report that some 6.5 million Italians are living under the poverty line. One family in four is poor in the south of the country, ISTAT said. (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
